# 周易參義

**ID:** KR1a0089
**Custom ID:** ZB1a0088
**Date (file):** 2015-08-24 21:57:14.224595
**Source:** 四庫全書 文淵閣版, V27.2, p195
**Extent:** 12 卷
**Base edition:** WYG

## Authors / Editors
- 梁寅 (元朝) 撰 1303 - 1389

**Editions:** WYG

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A Yuán-dynasty *Yìjīng* commentary in twelve juàn by Liáng Yín 梁寅 (1303–1389) of Xīnyú 新喻, completed in *zhì yuán* 至元 6 = 1340. Its method, signalled in the title, is to *cān* 參 — combine, triangulate — Chéng Yí's 程頤 *Yìchuán* 易傳 (which takes principle as its main concern) with Zhū Xī's 朱熹 *Běnyì* 本義 (which takes symbol-and-divination as its main concern), reconciling and merging the two into a single integrated reading and supplementing them with selected later glosses. The text follows the *gǔyì* 古易 division of upper and lower scripture and the ten Wings — the order Zhū Xī had adopted from Lǚ Zǔqiān's 呂祖謙 ([呂祖謙](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%91%82%E7%A5%96%E8%AC%99)) recovered base text. The *Sìkù* editors describe Liáng's exposition as plainspoken, anchored in everyday human conduct, neither lapsing into metaphysical vacuity nor straining for symbolic correspondences.

**Abstract**

Composition is firmly dated by the *Sìkù* notice to *zhì yuán* 6 = 1340 — Liáng's thirty-eighth year, well before the Yuán-Míng transition that would shape his later career. The dating bracket here therefore narrows to the year of completion. The work is among the more methodologically clean late-Yuán *Yì*-syntheses, taking as its explicit project the integration of the two principal Sòng commentaries — Chéng Yí's *Yìchuán* and Zhū Xī's *Běnyì* — that the more elaborate Hú Yīguì / Dǒng Zhēnqīng tradition had instead arranged in stratified layers (cf. [KR1a0086](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1a/KR1a0086)).

The *Sìkù* editors' assessment is moderately positive: they regard Liáng as honest, judicious, and clear, but stop short of treating him as an original *Yì*-thinker. The dating is also noteworthy for placing him in the same late-1340s generation as Qián Yìfāng ([KR1a0087](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1a/KR1a0087), 1346), Xiè Méng ([KR1a0084](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1a/KR1a0084)), and Chén Yìngrùn ([KR1a0088](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1a/KR1a0088), 1346) — a moment in late-Yuán *Yìxué* when the Hú Yīguì school synthesis (Dǒng Zhēnqīng's *Huìtōng*) had become available and four very different responses to it could appear within a half-decade.

Liáng's broader career — declining office at the Yuán-Míng transition, working briefly on the Hóngwǔ ritual reform, then returning to teach at Mount Shímén — places him squarely in the Yuán-loyalist Confucian milieu of late-fourteenth-century Jiāngxī, alongside such figures as Sòng Lián 宋濂 (whom he assisted at the Hóngwǔ court).
